about: Marks stay marked. Anything paid for wears a mark that says who, what and since when: beside the story, never in it. A mark buys a place, not a word. build-chapters.mjs shows each mark on the pages its routes name (a marked line under the slip, and schema.org sponsor in the page's structured data); book:check holds every mark to the policy. Nothing in the book is paid for today. It replaces patron-seals.json, whose open pedestals were pitches; an empty pedestal is now simply no mark.
policy: A mark is legible as patronage, never disguised as narration.
A mark keeps its provenance: who, for what, and since when.
A mark buys a place beside the story, never a word in it; editorial judgment stays with the scriptorium.
A mark's link is a marked threshold (rel="sponsored"), never a hidden door.
A mark never reaches the story's words, the audience gate, or a reader's own marks.

kinds.chapter: a chapter's printing, or a return route into one
kinds.route: a tool route or a page beside the story
kinds.snack: a treat Boof would approve, with a true label: who made it, what it costs, why it belongs near a working dog
kinds.recipe: a blueberry or boonberry recipe people can cook and share; food the story can stand next to

fields.id: a short name, lowercase with hyphens
fields.who: who it is from, as they would be named
fields.what: what it is for, one of the kinds: chapter, route, snack, recipe
fields.since: the date it was set, YYYY-MM-DD
fields.routes: the pages it stands beside, as paths (a chapter: /book/chapter/05/)
fields.url: where its link goes, https only
fields.words: the line shown beside the story, 120 characters at most
